newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor unveils major oil sands expansion.
newsitem.headline: Suncor unveils major oil sands expansion.

text.p: Suncor Energy Inc. unveiled aggressive plans on Thursday to invest C$2.2 billion ($1.6 billion) in its Canadian oil sands business to boost synthetic oil output to 210,000 barrels a day by 2002.

Calgary-based Suncor said the plan, called Project Millennium, would include expansions in two phases to oil sands extraction and upgrading facilities with the aim of increasing production by almost 250 percent from current levels.

The investment was in addition to C$600 million ($438 million) in expansion projects now under way at Suncor's oil sands facility near Fort McMurray in northeastern Alberta, the heart of Canada's vast oil sands reserves.
When the project reaches completion, the asset value of Suncor, Canada's fourth largest integrated oil company, will have doubled, Chief Executive Rick George told reporters.
Previous initiatives were aimed at bringing production to 105,000 barrels a day by 1999. Suncor's oil sands business now produces about 85,000 barrels a day.

"We have five growth priorities and future development of the oil sands business is No.1," George said. "Today's announcement really lays out the future we see for this business and how serious we are."

Canada's young oil sands industry -- which mines the bitumen, or very heavy oil, separates the petroleum from the sand and then upgrades it into light crude -- was already the target of billions of dollars worth of expansions and new projects by numerous companies over the next five years.
Oil from oil sands currently makes up about 20 percent of Canadian demand. Alberta is said to harbor more oil in the sands than Saudi Arabia's conventional reserves.

The announcement sent Suncor's stock soaring Thursday. Its shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange jumped C$7.10 to C$45.55, an increase of 18 percent. Suncor's New York Stock Exchange-listed shares rose $5.15625 to $33.25.

"I think we all expected that they would continue to expand oil sands, but I don't think we anticipated they would do it this soon and certainly not in this big a chunk," said Robert Hinckley, analyst with Merrill Lynch & Co. in New York.

The first phase of Project Millennium was a C$190 million ($139 million) investment in the existing plant. That work, to start immediately, would increase production to 130,000 barrels a day by 2001, said Suncor, whose current operation is Canada's second largest after Syncrude Canada Ltd.'s.
The second phase would be led off by a C$90 million ($66 million) technical, environmental and socioeconomic assessment to determine the best approach to the expansion.
When the study is complete, Suncor's board will make a final decision on the configuration of the full expansion and construction would start in 1999.
Suncor CEO George, who is credited with overseeing a major turnaround in the operation over the past five years, said the project would be funded by internal cash flow and debt.
The investment was expected to generate a return on capital greater than 15 percent, more than double that in the Canadian conventional oil and gas sector, he said.
Suncor kicked off Canada's oil sands era in 1967, and rejuvenated its operation five years ago by cutting costs with such initiatives as a switch to truck-and-shovel mining.

In other oil sands news Thursday, Shell Canada Ltd. announced a proposal to build a C$375 million ($274 million) pipeline to ship bitumen to Edmonton, Alberta, from its planned C$1 billion ($730 million) oil sands project near Fort McMurray.
The Corridor pipeline, which would tie into Shell Canada's Scotford Refinery, would be in operation by 2002, the same time frame as its own Lease 13 oil sands project.
